root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before the attacker-controlled count is used to size the read into info->missing_values, the program must establish that the count as parsed satisfies info->n_missing_values >= -3. The vulnerable program checks only the upper half (info->n_missing_values > 3) and does so after the abs() normalization at line 254, so it relies on abs() having already mapped every negative count to a non-negative one.
root_cause_criterion.description: The one-sided bound is the only guard between the parsed count and the size computation at line 262. For INT32_MIN the reliance on abs() fails, the signed comparison INT32_MIN > 3 is false, and the count is admitted. The fix commit supplies exactly this missing conjunct as `info->n_missing_values < -3` and moves the whole check ahead of the abs(), validating the count in the form it was parsed. Runtime evidence: the required assertion is violated in the vulnerable original (predicate false while the protected read executes) and guarded in the fixed original (predicate false, protected read never runs); the adjacent boundary case n_missing_values = -3 supplies the genuine witness in which the predicate holds and the protected read does execute.

nodes.state: The count reaching the `> 3` bound is still INT32_MIN, so the guard does not reject the record and control proceeds to the size computation.
free() is called on the value held in info->label after the non-NULL guard at line 78 admits it. The freed pointer is the corrupted, non-heap value rather than a pointer returned by readstat_malloc.

The overflowing copy changes info->label from the NULL left by readstat_calloc and the zero-length label path into a non-heap value assembled from trailing attacker bytes, breaking the ownership invariant that label is either NULL or allocator-owned.

The number of bytes memcpy'd into buf (which is info->missing_values) exceeds the 24-byte extent of that destination array, so the write runs past the destination and across the rest of the heap spss_varinfo_t.

abs() does not produce a non-negative result: +2147483648 is not representable in int, so the count is still INT32_MIN after the normalization the bounds check depends on. This is the only int32 value with this property.
The int32 n_missing_values field is materialized straight from attacker bytes as part of the packed 28-byte sav_variable_record_t, with no validation at the read site.
The unsatisfiable request turns the short read into READSTAT_ERROR_READ, so the very request that caused the overflow also guarantees the error path that frees the now-corrupted object.

The admitted count is sign-extended and multiplied by sizeof(double) to size a read into info->missing_values; the resulting request is vastly larger than the 24-byte extent of that destination, and the destination is never sized against the request at this call site.
The requested nbytes exceeds bytes_left, so the `nbytes <= bytes_left` branch is false and the truncated-copy branch is selected. Both branches bound the copy against the source buffer only.
The copy length equals bytes_left, the bytes remaining in the source buffer. The handler never consults the size of buf, so its contract silently assumes the caller sized the destination for nbytes.
The bytes actually copied are fewer than the requested byte count, which is the comparison the source performs to detect a short read.
The whole attacker input is aliased, not copied or validated, into the rt_buffer_t backing every io->read: buffer.used equals buffer.size, so the entire input remains available to later reads.

edges.relation: The exact pointer value written into info->label by the overflowing copy is the value later passed to free(). Verified by comparing the carried pointer values themselves, not their nullness.
The read into info->missing_values mutates info->label: the same source field differs immediately before and immediately after the responsible operation.
The length the handler actually copies exceeds the extent of the destination array supplied by the caller, which is what makes the write an overflow rather than a merely truncated read.
The oversized byte count computed at the call site is the same value the read handler receives as nbytes and tests against bytes_left.
The count that survived the bounds check is the same count that sizes the read, with no intervening clamp or revalidation.
abs() leaves the count unchanged: the same source value is identical immediately before and after the operation that is supposed to normalize it, which is why the later one-sided bound admits it.
The count crosses unchanged from the stack record into the heap spss_varinfo_t (ctx->bswap is 0), moving into the same object whose label field is later corrupted and freed.
The READSTAT_ERROR_READ produced by the short read is the same error value observed at the cleanup that calls spss_varinfo_free(info), so the corrupting path is the path that reaches the free.
